cards.text: Jehu, an army commander who was just anointed king over Israel, is plotting against Joram, Israel's king. Joram has gone back to Jezreel to recover from wounds the Arameans gave him in battle against Hazael, their king. Now Jehu has one order for the commanders who just shouted his name.

cards.question: Jehu tells his commanders that if they want him as king, someone should ride ahead and warn Jezreel.

cards.text: So Jehu hops in his chariot and heads for Jezreel, where Joram is laid up. Friend, this is a surprise visit, and NOT the kind with balloons.

cards.question: Someone has come down to Jezreel to see King Joram. Who is it?

cards.text: In Jezreel, a watchman on the tower spots Jehu's troops and calls out, "I see a company of troops!" King Joram tells him to choose a rider and send him out with a question.

cards.question: King Joram sends a rider out to meet the troops. What does Joram want him to ask them?

cards.text: The horseman rides up and asks, "Have you come in peace?" Jehu answers a yes or no question with a question: "What do you know about peace?"

cards.question: Jehu tells King Joram's horseman to ride back and give the king his answer.

cards.text: The watchman reports the rider reached them but isn't coming back, so Joram sends a second one, and Jehu gives him the exact same answer. That's like sending a coworker to find out what the boss wants, and they just NEVER come back to their desk.

cards.question: From the tower, the watchman can tell who's leading the troops just by the way he drives.

cards.text: The watchman says the charioteer drives like Jehu son of Nimshi: "he is driving like a madman!" Friend, when people can pick you out from a TOWER by how you drive, that's not a reputation, that's a warning label.

cards.question: King Joram hears that the driver coming at Jezreel drives like Jehu. What does Joram shout for?

answers.text: The city gates to be shut
His archers to man the wall

cards.text: Joram and Ahaziah ride out, each in his own chariot, and meet Jehu on the property of Naboth the Jezreelite. Naboth was the man Jezebel, King Ahab's wife, had killed so Ahab could take his vineyard (1 Kings 21:7-16).

cards.question: King Joram asks Jehu if he has come in peace. Jehu says there can't be peace as long as what goes on?

answers.text: The war with Hazael of Aram

cards.question: Jehu has just told King Joram there's no peace while Jezebel's idolatry goes on. Joram turns around and ___, calling out to Ahaziah.

cards.text: As he goes, Joram shouts, "Treachery, Ahaziah!" Then Jehu draws his bow and shoots Joram between the shoulders, and Joram slumps down in his chariot.

cards.question: Jehu tells Bidkar, his officer, to throw King Joram's body into the field of ___ the Jezreelite.

cards.text: Jehu reminds Bidkar of the day they rode behind Joram's father Ahab and the LORD lifted up a burden against him. The LORD had said, 'As surely as I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons yesterday, declares the LORD, so will I repay you on this plot of ground, declares the LORD.'

cards.question: Jehu says throwing Joram's body on that plot of ground follows the word of the LORD.

cards.text: Ahaziah, king of Judah, saw all of that, and friend, he does the math FAST. He flees up the road toward Beth-haggan, and Jehu goes after him.

cards.question: Jehu chases King Ahaziah of Judah up the road. What does Jehu shout?

cards.text: They shoot Ahaziah in his chariot on the Ascent of Gur, near Ibleam. He makes it to Megiddo and dies there.

cards.question: His servants carry King Ahaziah of Judah by chariot to ___ and bury him with his fathers.

cards.text: Quick note from the writer: Ahaziah had become king over Judah in the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab. Now Jehu arrives in Jezreel, and Jezebel hears about it.

cards.question: Jezebel hears that Jehu has arrived in Jezreel. What does she do?

answers.text: Paints her eyes and watches from a window
Hides in a room deep in the palace
Slips out of the city before dark

cards.text: As Jehu enters the gate, Jezebel asks if he's come in peace and calls him Zimri, murderer of his master. Zimri was a commander who killed his king, Elah, and reigned seven days (1 Kings 16:9-10, 15), which is less of a reign and more of a free trial.

cards.question: Jehu looks up at Jezebel's window and calls out, asking who is on his side.
Two or three eunuchs look down at Jehu from Jezebel's window. What does Jehu yell to them?

cards.text: So they throw her down. Her blood splatters on the wall and on the horses as they trample her underfoot.

cards.question: Right after Jezebel is thrown down, Jehu goes inside. What does he do there?
Jehu calls Jezebel a cursed woman but tells them to bury her, because she was the daughter of a ___.

cards.text: So they go out to bury her. Now remember what the young prophet told Jehu when he poured the oil: on the plot of ground at Jezreel, the dogs would devour Jezebel (2 Kings 9:10).

cards.question: When they go out to bury Jezebel, they find her whole body right where she fell.

cards.text: All they find is her skull, her feet and the palms of her hands. So they go back and tell Jehu, and he says this is the word of the LORD.

cards.question: Jehu says what happened to Jezebel is the word of the LORD. Through which servant had the LORD spoken it?
In the LORD's word through Elijah, Jezebel's body would lie in the field at Jezreel so that no one could say, This is Jezebel.

cards.text: And that's where the oven timer dings for now. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: This story card carries three moments: the watchman's report that the first rider isn't coming back, Joram sending a second rider, and Jehu giving him the same answer. Then a joke is added on top.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: Card 13 already tells the baker that Jehu meets Joram 'on the property of Naboth the Jezreelite' (v21). That gives away the answer to this fill in the blank, 'the field of ___ the Jezreelite.' The card ends up testing recall of a name the baker was just handed.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'Right after Jezebel is thrown down' adds an immediacy the text doesn't give. The BSB says only 'Then Jehu went in and ate and drank' (v34).

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line, as the docs allow when the last verse is asked on a choice card. It tells no verse, but it cites 2 Kings 9:37.
findings.question: What should a story card cite when it tells no verse, such as a closing 'story isn't over' line? Should it be the last verse, the verse asked on the card before, or null?
